correctness.rationale: The Gnedin–Olshanski Theorem 5.1 exact normalized double sum has terms (1-q)(q;q)_infty q^(rs+r+s)/((q;q)_r(q;q)_s). In the annulus q<|z|<q^-1, absolute convergence permits summing s first by Euler q-binomial and then r by the general q-binomial identity, obtaining (q;q)_infty^2/[(qz;q)_infty(q/z;q)_infty]. Each factor is the product of generating functions of independent geometric(q^k) variables, and their total expectations sum to a finite value, proving X-Xprime law. At z=-1 the parity difference is a convergent strictly positive product. Log differentiation on compact q-subintervals gives -4 Σ_{k>=1} k q^(k-1)/(1-q^(2k))<0, proving strict monotonicity and endpoints. Independent double-sum/product diagnostics at four q values agree to 1e-8. Those are corroborative; the q-binomial evaluation establishes the infinite law.

originality.rationale: Gnedin–Olshanski 2011 proves the exact one-point double-sum distribution, and this is explicitly an exact transform of that known marginal. He–Müller–Verstraaten 2022/2023 Section 10 explicitly leaves c_o>1/2>c_e for Q>1 as an open problem; this product gives its strict global solution and additionally monotonicity. The paper does NOT explicitly pose monotonicity as a second separate open problem, despite that wording in the assigned result; that attribution overstates the source, while both mathematical monotonicity and the explicitly posed parity inequality remain established. Bufetov–Chen 2024 uses a different nonergodic mixture measure.

value.rationale: The exact independent-geometric difference representation is a natural structural law for stationary single-site Mallows displacement and directly resolves a published open parity inequality. The strict monotonicity supplies additional global information, not just a computational reformulation of isolated values.

final_claim: For the balanced stationary two-sided q-Mallows permutation (0<q<1), its one-point displacement D has the law X-Xprime where X and Xprime are independent sums of geometric variables with parameter q^k; its bilateral generating function is the stated infinite Pochhammer product and its even-minus-odd parity gap is prod_{k>=1}((1-q^k)/(1+q^k))^2, strictly positive and strictly decreasing in q (hence even probability increasing in Q=1/q).
